title: Blood Relations & Direction Sense
relevance: Classic campus OA / aptitude questions that test careful reading, consistent modeling, and step-by-step deduction under time pressure.

phases.goal: Establish the standard notations and compass/shadow rules used to model these puzzles.

must_hit.point: Blood-relation diagrams use + for male, − for female; − for siblings, = for married couples, and | for parent–child.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states the gender marks and the three connection symbols for siblings, marriage, and parent–child.

must_hit.point: Direction-sense problems are drawn on standard N-E-S-W axes with North up, tracing each move as a vector relative to current facing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate sketches a compass with North up and explains left/right relative to facing, not absolute map sides alone.

must_hit.point: Morning: sun East, shadows West; evening: sun West, shadows East; left/right shadows imply facing North or South, front/back shadows imply East or West.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate recalls morning vs evening sun/shadow directions and links left/right vs front/back to axis facing.

probes: How do you notate gender and family links when drawing a blood-relation tree?
What are the morning and evening shadow rules, and what do they tell you about facing?

hints.1: Think about symbols for male/female and for sibling vs spouse vs parent.
hints.2: Separate diagram notation from direction/shadow rules: compass first, then sun position by time of day.
hints.3: Use +/− for gender; −/=/| for links; morning shadows West, evening East; left/right shadow ⇒ N/S facing.

phases.goal: Show how to resolve pointing statements, coded relation chains, and turn-by-turn paths without losing facing or gender constraints.

must_hit.point: For pointing/statement puzzles, work backwards from the speaker’s stated relation to identify the person.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate rewrites clauses inward (e.g., grandfather’s only son → father → that man’s daughter → sister).

must_hit.point: In coded blood relations, decode each operator left-to-right and do not assume the last person’s gender unless a symbol defines it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate traces each symbol for gender/role and explicitly says undefined genders stay unknown.

must_hit.point: After each left/right turn, re-orient facing before the next move; a left turn while facing South moves East on the map.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate updates facing after every turn and gives the South→left→East example.

must_hit.point: Shortest distance from start to end uses Pythagoras on net displacement (c² = a² + b²), not the sum of path segments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate nets North/South and East/West first, then applies c² = a² + b² for straight-line distance.

probes: Walk through: “She is the daughter of my grandfather’s only son.” Who is she to the speaker?
Why can “A is the brother of B” leave B’s gender unknown?
A walker faces South and turns left—which absolute direction do they go next?

hints.1: Reduce nested phrases one clause at a time from the inside.
hints.2: For codes, list what each operator forces about gender; for paths, track facing after every turn.
hints.3: Grandfather’s only son = father → daughter = sister; brother-of leaves other gender open; South + left = East.

phases.goal: Contrast modeling choices that change the answer: displacement vs path length, and defined vs assumed gender/relation.

must_hit.point: Prefer net displacement (and Pythagoras when needed) for “how far from start” over totaling the walked length.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate distinguishes “distance from starting point” as resultant vector length, citing c² = a² + b² when axes are perpendicular.

must_hit.point: Prefer relations forced by symbols/statements over filling maternal/paternal or gender gaps the puzzle never states.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate refuses to invent gender or maternal vs paternal when the chain does not specify it.

probes: If a question asks how far someone is from the start after several legs, do you add the kilometers or compute displacement—and why?
When is it wrong to decide someone’s gender or whether an uncle is maternal vs paternal?

hints.1: “How far from start” is usually about position, not odometer.
hints.2: Compare summing path length with netting coordinates, then check what each coded symbol actually asserts.
hints.3: Use net a,b then c² = a² + b²; leave gender/in-law side open unless a symbol or statement fixes it.

phases.goal: Apply the methods to multi-generation counts, coded chains, and OA-style path/shadow problems with checkable answers.

must_hit.point: In the six-person family puzzle, C (wife of B, mother of F) is the mother of A once B–C’s children are A and F.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate builds generations: D grandmother, E grandfather, B–C couple, A and F children ⇒ C mother of A.

must_hit.point: Female count in the joint-family OA: wife (1) + three sons’ wives (3) + two unmarried daughters (2) + four granddaughters (2×2) = 10.
Coded chain P @ Q $ M # T makes P the grandfather of T (P husband of Q, Q mother of M, M father of T).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate decodes each operator and concludes grandfather.

must_hit.point: Path nets to (3, 4) after 10 km North, 6 km South, 3 km East ⇒ √(3² + 4²) = 5 km North-East of start.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate nets 4 km North and 3 km East, then states 5 km North-East.

probes: How many female members are in the joint family with three married sons and the stated grandchildren?
Decode P @ Q $ M # T: how is P related to T?
After 10 km North, 6 km South, and 3 km East, how far and in which direction from the start?

hints.1: Count females by generation; decode operators in order; net N/S then E/W.
hints.2: Joint family: 1 + 3 + 2 + (2×2); P is father of M who is father of T; nets are +4 North and +3 East.
hints.3: Females = 10; P is grandfather; distance = 5 km North-East.

tradeoffs.topic: Straight-line displacement vs total path length
tradeoffs.strong_answer: “How far from the starting point” means net displacement; net the N/S and E/W components, then use Pythagoras (c² = a² + b²) when needed—do not sum every leg unless asked for distance walked.

tradeoffs.topic: Defined gender/relation vs assumed gender or maternal/paternal side
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Only take gender and maternal/paternal facts the statement or code symbol forces; e.g. “A is brother of B” does not fix B’s gender, and in-law chains should not invent maternal vs paternal when unspecified.

gotchas.trap: Assuming the gender of the last person in a coded chain when the symbol only defines the first person’s role (e.g. A + B as A brother of B leaves B’s gender unknown).
gotchas.correction: Assign gender only when a symbol or explicit word requires it; leave the other person unspecified otherwise.

gotchas.trap: Treating in-law or uncle/aunt chains as maternal or paternal when the puzzle never says which side.
gotchas.correction: State only what is forced (e.g. uncle) and avoid maternal vs paternal unless the wording establishes it.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting current facing after a turn so left/right are applied on the wrong absolute axis (e.g. left while facing South should go East).
gotchas.correction: After every turn, update facing first, then move; always re-orient the mental compass before the next vector.
